assembly.review_scope: Actual uninstrumented rowsix/helper fragment. Root independently reviews all actual conv2d/outlined dispatch functions before merging. No production object is retained; no performance or old-C40 machine-code identity claim.

helpers.stack_frame_description: Fixed672-byte frame created by SUB sp,sp,#672 at5708; no scalable ADDVL/RDVL allocation. D8..D15 low64-bit ABI preservation uses four STP/LDP pairs atsp+112/+128/+144/+160. Other stack contents are saved X/W registers, scalar dimensions and external pointer locals/outgoing arguments.
helpers.spill_count_scope: Static Z/Q/predicate spill instruction sites across the entire5705..6869 helper, including non-loop setup and exits. D-register ABI saves are excluded. These are not dynamic memory-operation totals.
helpers.spill_notes: No Z/Q or predicate LDR/STR and no vector LD/ST through a stack-derived address are present. The only constructed SP alias is x29=sp+16; it never feeds a vector memory instruction. Scalar stack slots176..368 and376..664 contain dimensions or pointers derived from base/kernel/dst arguments plus row/column offsets. Loading an external pointer from one of those slots does not make the subsequent input LD1W, coefficient LD1RW or output ST1W a stack spill. All24 accumulators remain in Z registers, including the transition from leading input4 to the six-row shared phase and all five trailing phases.
helpers.transition_spill_review: Read all5705..6869. Leading loops initialize each new output row in registers, and phase transitions reload only scalar external row/kernel pointers. .L3946211 sets t=5, initializes f and loads shared kernel bases x4/x5/x6/x7/x8/x11 for rows5/4/3/2/1/0. .L4066231 constructs first input base x12=x3-oneVL_bytes; x3/x10/x9 are the other three vector bases. .L4046306 increments t and all six kernel bases by4*kw, advances input-row pointers by4*stride, and branches back until t==kh. Every subsequent trailing phase completes an earlier output row and preserves its Z accumulators until the24 ST1W stores in .L4076544. The horizontal bookkeeping uses only integer locals. .L4196713 initializes the20 leading accumulators on kw<=0 then joins .L394; no skipped-loop vector is left uninitialized or stored in a stack slot. No live output accumulator crosses fallback calls.
helpers.tail_and_fallback_review: CMP kh,5 / BLE .L391 precedes full six-row setup; .L3916819..6851 calls rowquad for outputs0..3, then tail-branches rowpair at base+4*stride for outputs4/5 with original width. Full tiles require ow-i >= CNTB, numerically4*svcntw float outputs; INCB advances the output-column count by that exact block and pointer step x17 is four times that count in bytes. The width-small .L4436852 path sets i=0 and joins .L393. Positive horizontal remainder goes through .L4446756, rowquad at column i then rowpair at row4,column i, using original input stride and distinct dst pointers. The vector path restores d8..d15 before tail dispatch, while width-small/kh<6 branches precede those saves. Each of the eleven phases uses ik=0; ik++ and signed CMP/BGT kw, so kw=1 and odd/even widths follow the same single-column loop. The last full input vector starts at i+3*lanes+ik and ends i+4*lanes+ik-1 <= ow+kw-2. Last input row kh+4 is exactly required by output5. Each output sees kernel rows0..kh-1 and columns0..kw-1 in order, with separate multiplication and addition.
helpers.arithmetic_and_load_review: Shared .L4056237..6305 is68 actual instructions per kernel column:24 ordinary FMUL,24 FADD,4 input LD1W,6 LD1RW coefficient broadcasts,1 LSL,7 ADD,1 CMP and1 BGT. No indexed FMUL/LD1RQW/DUP/EXT/MOVPRFX/vector MOV or spill there. Four input windows are held as z3,z2,z1,z0; GCC processes their contributions mainly by output row and reuses coefficient/product temporaries z12..z15, rather than retaining six coefficient vectors simultaneously. The final row consumes input registers in place only after earlier rows have used them. Leading/trailing static arithmetic counts are4/8/12/16/20 and20/16/12/8/4 FMUL plus equal FADD, four input loads and1..5/5..1 coefficient broadcasts. This explains observed register allocation only, not a hardware-throughput or speedup conclusion.

helpers.whole_helper_count_scope: Static function instruction sites, not per-call dynamic totals: shared repeats across input rows and all phases across kw. Complete actual function has24 final ST1W output stores. Ordinary stack bookkeeping and ABI traffic contribute to the total instruction count.

dispatch_functions.control_flow_notes: Actual legacy per-output-row worker: omp thread quotient/remainder assigns disjoint row intervals at .L58/.L141; .L67 advances input by stride and output by ow. Context flag at +48 optionally calls prefix at .L60, then returned column offset enters remaining 32/16/8/4/2/1 output blocks (.L123/.L109/.L63/.L64/.L65/.L66). Non-SVE context stores flag zero in conv2d, so this runtime branch does not call SVE. Ordered kernel rows/columns and scalar-tail stores observed through .L76. No new six-row dispatch enters this path.
dispatch_functions.stack_notes: Actual 368-byte fixed frame. x19..x30 ABI and scalar/pointer loop state at sp160..232; d8..d15 four STP/LDP ABI pairs at sp96..144. x18=sp240 aliases the local 32-float tile: zeroed sp240..352 then 8+4+2 STR Q sites materialize computed 32/16/8 blocks, subsequently copied via scalar LDP/STP. These 14 vector tile-store sites are real stack traffic, distinct from hot SVE accumulator spill and ABI saves. No Z/predicate stack access in this function; all non-SVE scalar and NEON paths reviewed.

dispatch_functions.control_flow_notes: Legacy SVE groups of four use signed quotient/remainder partition at .L446/.L454; current row is group*4, input advances four strides and output four ow. .L450 routes remaining>=4 to rowquad, 3 to rowtriple .L451, 2 to rowpair .L452, 1 to prefix. All return through .L453, increment group once, subtract remaining by4 and compare assigned group end; no overlap or skipped remainder observed.
dispatch_functions.stack_notes: 160-byte frame, integer ABI x19..x30 saves; outgoing rowquad/triple arguments at sp0..8, end/index/weight pointer and output strides at sp124..152. No vector/predicate stack transfers. Full entry, rare branches and epilogues reviewed.

dispatch_functions.control_flow_notes: New six-row worker uses unsigned quotient/remainder over ceil(oh/6) groups at .L461/.L471; .L465 calls rowsix only when remaining>5. Remaining5 at .L466 calls quad for first four and prefix at input+4*stride/output+4*ow; remaining4/3/2/1 use quad/triple/pair/prefix at .L467/.L468/.L469/default. .L470 increments group once, subtracts6 from remaining, advances input by6*stride and each output pointer by6*ow before next assigned-group boundary. rowsix receives six consecutive output addresses via x5/x6/x7 and sp0/8/16 plus width sp24. Context arithmetic uses 64-bit group indices, disjoint output ownership preserved.
dispatch_functions.stack_notes: 208-byte fixed frame, x19..x30 integer ABI saved at sp32..128. Outgoing args sp0..24, scalar width at132 and saved end/pointers/strides sp136..200; no Z/Q/predicate transfers or D ABI saves. The extra prefix for rem5 preserves first output/next-row pointers at168/192 correctly. Full paths and epilogues reviewed.

dispatch_functions.control_flow_notes: Rejects nonpositive kh/kw before frame, rejects kernels larger than input via .L477. Computes oh/ow once, obtains HWCAP bit4194304. Six-row context .L487 only when SVE present and kh>5 and oh>5. Uses constant-multiply division by6 plus remainder to construct ceil(oh/6), stores 64-bit oh/ow and original stride. SVE with smaller kh/oh falls to ceil(oh/4) old .omp_fn.1 at .L480. Absent SVE uses .omp_fn.2 with context flag0 via .L479. Each path invokes exactly one GOMP_parallel and rejoins/restores before return; no copies, allocator, cache or extra timing region introduced.
dispatch_functions.stack_notes: 160-byte frame, integer ABI and stack context at sp88..152; no vector/predicate memory access. Context fields match worker loads; no access beyond allocated frame. Early no-op return and every post-GOMP restore observed.
